title: Architecture & Standards: API, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance + ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This page consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards: API design, coding and repo hygiene, infrastructure/IaC, model-serving contracts, observability, and performance targets. It also summarizes recent ADRs that affect these domains. The goal is to provide engineers and product stakeholders with a single reference for design decisions and operational requirements that preserve reliability, security, and cost-effectiveness across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope
- Applies to all new services, public-facing API surfaces, and model-serving integrations.
- Recommendations for migration of legacy services are provided in the "Migration guidance" section.

Principles (applied to all standards)
- Consistency: Use shared libraries, modules, and templates so cross-service behavior is predictable.
- Observable by default: Instrumentation, structured logs, and dashboards must be included in PRs for new services.
- Production-first: All changes must be safe to roll back and have automated canary testing for major releases.
- Cost-awareness: Design choices should include unit cost impact (tokens/second, GPU-hours).

1) API standards (owner: API Platform)
Intro: Public and internal APIs must follow a common contract pattern so SDKs, routing policies, and rate-limiting behave predictably.

Design guidelines:
- API style: REST + JSON for public endpoints; gRPC is allowed for high-throughput internal service-to-service communication (see ADR-2024-01).
- Versioning: Use semantic major version in the path: /v1/, /v2/. Non-breaking additions use minor versions in the spec and are backward compatible.
- Idempotency: All state-changing operations must accept an Idempotency-Key header and be idempotent within 24 hours.
- Pagination: cursor-based pagination with opaque cursor tokens. Responses MUST include next_cursor and page_size metadata.
- Errors: Use structured error objects: {"code": "INTERNAL_ERROR", "message": "...", "details": []}. Prefer narrow error codes (AUTHZ_DENIED, RATE_LIMITED, MODEL_TIMEOUT).
- Rate limiting: Per-route rate limiting with pluggable quota tiers. Public token default: 60 requests/minute. Critical system routes may have higher limits defined in route config.
- Authentication: Bearer tokens (JWT) for internal services; API keys for public consumption. All tokens must be verified against central auth service and logged (token id only) for audit.
- Response contract: Responses SHOULD include a standard meta object with request_id, model_tag, cost_estimate_tokens, and processing_time_ms.

Examples (request/response)
Request (JSON):
{
  "input": "Summarize the following...",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "temperature": 0.2
}
Response (JSON):
{
  "request_id": "r-01F...",
  "model_tag": "gpt-redwood-1.0",
  "meta": {"processing_time_ms": 412, "cost_estimate_tokens": 320},
  "output": "...summary..."
}

Backward compatibility checklist for API changes:
1. Additive changes allowed without version bump (new optional fields)
2. Removing or renaming fields requires a major version bump and a migration plan
3. Deprecation window: minimum 90 days with telemetry-based adoption tracking

2) Coding & repo standards (owner: Developer Experience)
- Languages supported: Go (core platform services), Python (model-serving and eval tooling), TypeScript (console and SDKs).
- Formatting & linting: Enforce gofmt/golangci-lint, black + ruff for Python, and ESLint + Prettier for TypeScript via pre-commit hooks.
- Type coverage: Python services must use mypy with strictness level "basic" at minimum. TypeScript projects must enable --strict in tsconfig.
- Testing: Unit tests >= 80% coverage for critical libraries; integration tests required for any public API route. All tests run in CI with parallel matrix across supported runtimes.
- Branching & PRs: Small, focused PRs. Feature branches must include a description, a test plan, and an ownership tag in the PR body (owner: @team/name).
- Security checks: SCA scanning, secret scanning, and SAST run in CI before merge.

3) Infrastructure & IaC standards (owner: Eng Infra)
- Terraform modules: Use the central terraform-modules repo. Modules must be published with semantic version tags and reviewed by infra owners before usage.
- Environment topology: dev -> staging -> prod. IaC changes must be tested in staging and validated by integration smoke tests.
- Resource tagging: All resources must include tags: {owner_team, service, cost_center, environment, compliance}.
- Networking: VPC per-tenant for Private deployments; shared VPC with strict namespace isolation for Hosted. Default network ACLs deny all inbound traffic except required ports.
- Secrets & keys: KMS/HSM usage for Private deployments; secrets stored in central secrets manager with restricted RBAC. Rotate keys annually or on compromise.
- Capacity planning: GPU fleet autoscaling policies are defined in gpu-fleet-and-capacity runbook. Minimum capacity must allow 99th percentile expected burst for 15 minutes.

4) Model-serving standards (owner: Applied ML & Serving Runtime)
Contract & packaging:
- Model bundle format: tar.gz with manifest.json including model_id, architecture, quantization_profile, tokenizer_version, expected_max_length, and sha256.
- Size expectations: Provide guidance per deployment class: Hosted: models up to 30B with quantization; Dedicated: up to 70B depending on customer cluster; Private: customer-by-customer.
- Quantization & kernels: Include recommended quantization profile from quantization-profiles directory; document fallback to full-precision path in manifest.
- KV cache contract: Cache keys must be deterministic based on prompt prefix and model_tag; cache TTLs default to 24 hours unless specified in manifest.

Quality & validation:
- CI validation: Model pull request must include perf profile (latency, memory, throughput), a small eval on representative prompt set, and a canary rollout plan.
- Regression checks: Any model update must run regression evals against baseline prompt sets with automatic blocking thresholds (see quality-guardrails).

Runtime behavior:
- Failure modes: Model-serving must support graceful degradation: fallback to smaller or older model variant, or batched error responses with retry-after headers.
- Idempotency: Generation requests that alter model state (e.g., fine-tune jobs) must be idempotent and use Idempotency-Key.

5) Observability standards (owner: Eng Platform)
Metrics:
- Metrics naming: follow prometheus naming conventions service_<name>_<metric>_<unit>. Include labels: service, owner_team, environment, model_tag.
- Required metrics for all services: request_count, request_latency_ms_bucket (histogram), error_count, cpu_utilization_percent, memory_bytes. For model-serving add: tokens_generated_total, kv_cache_hit_ratio, batch_size_distribution.

Tracing & logs:
- Distributed tracing: Instrument top-level request trace with root span containing model_tag and request_id. Traces should be sampled at 100% in staging and 10% in prod by default.
- Logs: Structured JSON logs with fields {timestamp, level, service, request_id, user_id (if applicable), message, err}. PII must be redacted.

Dashboards & alerts:
- Dashboards: Each service must ship a per-route dashboard with p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, throughput, and cost per request.
- Alerting thresholds (recommended defaults):
  - High error rate: error_rate > 1% for 5m -> SEV-2
  - Elevated latency: p95 > SLO_latency_threshold for 10m -> SEV-2
  - Capacity pressure: GPU_utilization > 85% for 10m -> paging to oncall
- Oncall runbooks: Link runbooks to playbooks and postmortem templates.

6) Performance standards (owner: Eng SRE + Serving Runtime)
Service classes and SLOs (example):
- Interactive generation (low-latency): p50 < 100ms per token, p95 < 600ms total for typical short prompts (<=256 tokens), target availability 99.9%
- Batch embedding and offline jobs: throughput-oriented; target throughput 10k embeddings/min per dedicated worker, job success rate 99.5%
- High-throughput streaming: p50 per-chunk latency < 50ms, p95 < 200ms
- Cold-start SLO: 95% of model starts complete in < 30s in Dedicated pools.

Performance engineering guidelines:
- Batching: Configure dynamic batching with target latency budgets; prefer micro-batching on high QPS routes, and set max_batch_size per model in runtime config.
- Caching: Prefix/KV cache recommended for repeated prompt prefixes; measure cache_hit_ratio and ensure cache TTLs balance correctness and cost.
- Quantization & kernels: Use quantized paths for production traffic where quality regressions are within documented thresholds.
- Load testing: New service or model rollout must include load tests that reproduce expected p95 targets using realistic prompt distributions.

Measurement & reporting:
- Monthly performance report: Each service owner publishes a monthly performance summary with SLO attainment, cost per 1k tokens, and recent regressions.

7) Decision Records (ADRs)
ADR-2024-01: Internal gRPC for high-throughput service-to-service communication
- Date: 2024-02-28
- Decision: Adopt gRPC with protobuf for internal high-throughput services (model-routing, tokenization, and batch orchestration) while keeping REST/JSON for public-facing APIs.
- Rationale: gRPC provides lower latency and smaller payloads for internal RPCs, enabling better throughput between runtime components. REST remains easier for external integrations and human-readable debugging.
- Consequences: Need to maintain language bindings and central proto registry. CI must enforce backwards compatibility checks on proto changes (breaking changes require ADR and migration plan).
- Owner: Eng Platform

ADR-2024-05: Default model quantization policy
- Date: 2024-08-12
- Decision: Use 8-bit quantization profiles as default for Hosted deployments where latency/cost benefits exceed measured quality regressions. Dedicated and Private deployments can opt into higher-precision paths.
- Rationale: Unit costs and throughput improvements make quantization the default for cost-sensitive workloads. We require regression evals as part of the model onboarding flow.
- Owner: Applied ML & Evals

ADR-2025-01: Standard request_id propagation and sampling policy
- Date: 2025-01-09
- Decision: Enforce a standardized request_id header across all services and adopt a default tracing sample rate of 10% in prod, 100% in staging.
- Owner: Eng Platform

Migration guidance and enforcement
- New services: Use the service template repo which wires in CI, linting, instrumentation, and Terraform module scaffolding. PRs that introduce services are required to include a completed checklist (tests, metrics, dashboard, runbook link).
- Existing services: Follow provided compatibility checklist and schedule migrations during low-traffic windows; notify owners at least 30 days in advance for breaking changes.
- Enforcement: CI gates validate linting, tests, proto compatibility, and presence of required metrics. Security/infra owners may block merging when critical rules fail.

Ownership and review cadence
- Each standard has an owning team listed above. Standards are reviewed quarterly by a cross-functional Architecture Review Board (ARB) consisting of representatives from Eng Infra, Eng Platform, Applied ML, Eng SRE, and DX.

References and related pages
- API versioning: confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/api-versioning-guidelines-2024
- Model onboarding checklist: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/model-onboarding-checklist-2024
- Quantization profiles: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profiles-2024
- Runtime architecture: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture

Appendix: checklist for PRs touching standards
- Add/verify metrics and dashboards
- Add or update runbook entries
- Ensure CI includes linting, tests, and proto compatibility checks
- Add performance regression tests or load tests as needed
- Add or update ADR if change is architectural and irreversible

Change log
- 2024-02-28: ADR-2024-01 added (gRPC decision).
- 2024-08-12: ADR-2024-05 recorded (quantization default).
- 2025-01-09: ADR-2025-01 recorded (request_id propagation).

Contact
- For questions or changes, open a PR in the architecture repo and tag the ARB reviewers, or contact @aisha.patel (Architecture owner).
